models.statusMeaning: Findings are computed and shown to programme staff for review only. They create no tasks, messages, flags on cases or protocol changes.
models.owner: FEMOS engineering team (prototype); clinical owner to be appointed by the district programme before any pilot

method.individual: Per woman, readings in the previous 12 months. TREND: ≥3 readings spanning ≥60 days, Theil–Sen slope ≤ −0.1 g/dL/month and projected Hb < 8.0 g/dL within 6 months. DROP: mean of latest two readings ≥1.5 g/dL below the earlier personal max. Women severe at their first reading are excluded.
method.school: Monthly share of readings below the WHO 2024 cut-off by age (<11.5 g/dL at 10–11 y, <12.0 g/dL at 12+ y) vs the unit's own first-9-month baseline (Beta-shrunk to the pooled baseline, prior weight 20). One-sided upper CUSUM on monthly binomial z, k=0.5, h=4, months with <5 readings skipped.
method.block: Referral follow-up completion by referral month (complete cohorts only: month end + 30 days ≤ asOf) vs own baseline. One-sided lower CUSUM, k=0.5, h=4, min 5 per month.
method.device: OCR rejection rate per device model vs all other models pooled, cumulative: two-proportion z ≥ 4, rate ratio ≥ 1.5, ≥100 photos.
method.process: Referral stall rate (no follow-up within 30 days) per district × touchpoint vs all other referrals, cumulative: two-proportion z ≥ 3.5, rate ratio ≥ 1.5, ≥40 resolved referrals.

models.thresholdPolicy: Chosen once from first principles (WHO severe cut-off, conventional CUSUM k/h, Bonferroni-style z for multiple cells) before the evaluation was run. Not tuned per seed. Any change is a new version and must be re-evaluated on all seeds.

trainingData.note: Nothing is fitted; the synthetic data is used only to evaluate the fixed rules against planted patterns. No real patient data has been used.

evaluation.command: npm run synth && npm run learn
evaluation.noPeeking: Evaluated month by month (mineIncremental); a referral outcome is visible only once it has happened or its 30-day deadline has passed.

biasChecks.acceptance: Before leaving shadow mode, recall and false-alarm rate must not differ between groups by more than an agreed margin on real retrospective data, reviewed by the clinical owner.
notChecked: caste/community, religion, income or disability (not recorded in the synthetic data)
differences in visit frequency driven by access

limitations: Evaluated only on synthetic data with planted patterns generated by the same team that wrote the miner; real-world performance is unknown.
Individual flags need ≥3 readings in 12 months; women seen rarely (often the most underserved) cannot be flagged. Recall is limited by visit frequency, not only by the rule.
School/village prevalence monitoring is slow with ~7 readings per school per month: median delay of several months, with misses and false alarms.
Process and device signals are cumulative two-proportion tests: they detect persistent differences, not short episodes, and become significant only after enough referrals accumulate.
WHO cut-offs are applied without altitude, smoking or pregnancy adjustment.
A flag means 'look here sooner', never 'this woman is ill' or 'this team is failing'.

changelog.change: Initial shadow rule set and synthetic evaluation.

models.regulatoryNote: If findings were used to direct individual patient care, the software could be Software as a Medical Device (SaMD) under India's Medical Devices Rules 2017 (CDSCO) and comparable regimes. It is kept in shadow mode, for population/programme review, until a qualified clinical owner, an ethics process and the applicable regulator have reviewed it.
